why: I checked all six verifier checks against their expect lines. Each PASS/FAIL condition stays within what the words require. Check 1 tests the `<file>:<line>: <error>` prefix, 1-based numbers, blank lines skipped, the torn last row and exit codes 1/0. Check 2 needs only exit 2 with non-empty stderr; it adds no stdout rule. Check 3 asks for a named `lint` export returning `[{line, error}]`. Its `line` 2 value is just the 1-based line from expect line 1, not an extra rule. Check 4 tests the name, type, test script, no dependencies and the five test scenarios; "tests pass" is already required by expect line 6. Check 5 needs a non-empty README and a root README mention. Check 6 tests one PR, the Closes line, and npm test plus the workflow green at the head. The stricter items (shebang, executable bit, CRLF input, "no tools" text removed) all sit under "Advisory", which says "These are not pass/fail conditions."
